references.text: Isaiah compares God's word to rain and snow that fall down and cause the earth to sprout and grow – a parallel to the image of the seed as God's word in Jesus' parable.

Matthew's version of Jesus' explanation of the Parable of the Sower, where the seed represents 'the word about the kingdom' and the different types of soil represent various ways of receiving God's word.
Mark's version of the explanation of the Parable of the Sower, where the sower sows 'the word' – a direct parallel to Luke's formulation that the seed is God's word.
The parable itself as explained in Luke 8:11. Jesus tells about a sower who scatters seed that falls on different types of soil.
Peter uses the same image: believers are born again through God's living and enduring word, like an imperishable seed. God's word is compared to a seed with life-giving power.
James urges people to receive 'the word planted in you' with humility – an image that connects to the seed metaphor for God's word.
John uses the image of God's seed (σπέρμα) remaining in those born of God – a parallel to the idea of God's word as a seed that bears fruit in the believer.
Moses says: 'Like rain my teaching shall drop, like dew my words shall flow.' God's word is compared to something that falls down and brings growth, similar to the seed image.
The crowd pressed in on Jesus to hear 'the word of God' (τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ) – the same expression used in Luke 8:11 for what the seed represents.
'The word of God was growing' – this expression shows that God's word grows and bears fruit, consistent with the image of a seed sprouting and producing a harvest.
